readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Appointed Times of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Weekly Sabbath
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘The appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which you are to proclaim as set-apart gatherings, <dn>My</dn> appointed times, are these:</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six days work is done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of rest, a set-apart gathering. You do no work, it is a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in all your dwellings.</dq> [4] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, set-apart gatherings which you are to proclaim at their appointed times.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Festival of Passover and Matzot
readings.subtitle: The First of the Annual Feasts
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:5] <dq>‘In the first new moon, on the fourteenth day of the new moon, between the evenings, is the Pěsaḥ to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And on the fifteenth day of this new moon is the Festival of Matzot to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – seven days you eat unleavened bread.</dq> [7] <dq>‘On the first day you have a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the seventh day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Offering of First-fruits
readings.subtitle: The Sheaf of the Wave Offering
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [10] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and you shall say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, and shall reap <dn>את</dn> its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits of your harvest to the priest.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And <dn>he</dn> shall wave <dn>את</dn> the sheaf before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for your acceptance. On the morrow after the Sabbath the priest waves it.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And on that day when you wave the sheaf, you shall prepare a male lamb a year old, a perfect one, as an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [13] <dq>and its grain offering: two-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a sweet fragrance, and its drink offering: one-fourth of a hin of wine.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And you do not eat bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the same day that you have brought <dn>את</dn> an offering to your <dn>Elohim</dn> – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Festival of Weeks
readings.subtitle: Counting Fifty Days to Shavuot
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:15] <dq>‘And from the morrow after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought <dn>את</dn> the sheaf of the wave offering, you shall count for yourselves: seven completed Sabbaths.</dq> [16] <dq>‘Until the morrow after the seventh Sabbath you count fifty days, then you shall bring a new grain offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>‘Bring from your dwellings for a wave offering two loaves of bread, of two-tenths of an ěphah of fine flour they are, baked with leaven, first-fruits to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And besides the bread, you shall bring seven lambs a year old, perfect ones, and one young bull and two rams. They are an ascending offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And you shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old, as a slaughter of peace offerings.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And the priest shall wave them, besides the bread of the first-fruits, as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, besides the two lambs. They are set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the priest.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And on this same day you shall proclaim a set-apart gathering for yourselves, you do no servile work on it – a law forever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And when you reap <dn>את</dn> the harvest of your land do not completely reap the corners of your field when you reap, and do not gather any gleaning from your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the stranger. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Festival of Trumpets
readings.subtitle: A Remembrance of Teru'ah
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [24] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘In the seventh new moon, on the first day of the new moon, you have a rest, a remembrance of Teru‛ah, a set-apart gathering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘You do no servile work, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Day of Atonement
readings.subtitle: A Sabbath of Rest and Affliction
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [27] <dq>“On the tenth day of this seventh new moon is Yom haKippurim. It shall be a set-apart gathering for you. And you shall afflict your beings, and shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“And you do no work on that same day, for it is Yom Kippurim, to make atonement for you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>“For any being who is not afflicted on that same day, <dn>he</dn> shall be cut off from <dn>his</dn> people.</dq> [30] <dq>“And any being who does any work on that same day, that being <dn>I</dn> shall destroy from the midst of <dn>his</dn> people.</dq> [31] <dq>“You do no work – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq> [32] <dq>‘It is a Sabbath of rest to you, and you shall afflict your beings. On the ninth day of the new moon at evening, from evening to evening, you observe your Sabbath.”</dq>

footnotes.Foonote: Day of Atonement or Day of the Coverings.

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Festival of Booths
readings.subtitle: Dwelling in Sukkot for Seven Days
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [34] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh new moon is the Festival of Sukkot for seven days to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [35] <dq>‘On the first day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [36] <dq>‘For seven days you bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. On the eighth day there shall be a set-apart gathering for you, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a closing festival, you do no servile work.</dq> [37] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you proclaim as set-apart gatherings, to bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, an ascending offering and a grain offering, a slaughtering and drink offerings, as commanded for every day –</dq> [38] <dq>besides the Sabbaths of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your voluntary offerings which you give to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh new moon, when you gather in the fruit of the land, celebrate the festival of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day a rest.</dq> [40] <dq>‘And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of good trees, branches of palm trees, twigs of leafy trees, and willows of the stream, and shall rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for seven days.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And you shall celebrate it as a festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days in the year – a law forever in your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh new moon.</dq> [42] <dq>‘Dwell in booths for seven days; all who are native born in Yisra’ěl dwell in booths,</dq> [43] <dq>so that your generations know that <dn>I</dn> made the children of Yisra’ěl dwell in booths when <dn>I</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [44] Thus did Mosheh speak of the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: The Lampstand and the Bread of Presence
readings.subtitle: Continual Service in the Tent of Appointment
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>"Command the children of Yisra’ěl that they bring to you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.</dq> [3] <dq>“Outside the veil of the Witness, in the Tent of Appointment, Aharon is to arrange it from evening until morning before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually – a law forever throughout your generations.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> is to arrange the lamps on the clean gold lampstand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually.</dq> [5] <dq>“And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it, two-tenths of an ěphah in each cake.</dq> [6] <dq>“And you shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the clean table before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“And you shall put clear frankincense on each row, and it shall be on the bread as a remembrance portion, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“On every Sabbath <dn>he</dn> is to arrange it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually, from the children of Yisra’ěl – an everlasting covenant.</dq> [9] <dq>“And it shall be for Aharon and <dn>his</dn> sons, and they shall eat it in the set-apart place, because it is most set-apart to <dn>him</dn> from the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire – an everlasting law.”</dq>

readings.title: The Penalty for Blasphemy
readings.subtitle: One Right-Ruling for the Native and the Stranger
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:10] And the son of an Yisra’ěli woman, whose father was a Mitsrian man, went out among the children of Yisra’ěl. And the Yisra’ěli woman’s son and a man of Yisra’ěl strove in the camp. [11] And the Yisra’ěli woman’s son blasphemed <dn>את</dn> the Name, and cursed. So they brought him to Mosheh. Now his mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Diḇri, of the tribe of Dan. [12] And they put him under guard, that it might be declared to them at the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [14] <dq>“Bring <dn>את</dn> the one who has cursed outside the camp, and all those who heard <dn>him</dn> shall lay their hands on <dn>his</dn> head, and all the congregation shall stone <dn>him</dn>.</dq> [15] <dq>“And speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘Anyone who curses <dn>his</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bear <dn>his</dn> sin.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And <dn>he</dn> who blasphemes the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly be put to death, and all the congregation certainly stone <dn>him</dn>, the stranger as well as the native. When <dn>he</dn> blasphemes the Name, <dn>he</dn> is put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And a man who strikes the being of any man shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And <dn>he</dn> who strikes a beast repays it, body for body.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And when a man inflicts a blemish upon <dn>his</dn> neighbour, as <dn>he</dn> has done so it is done to <dn>him</dn>:</dq> [20] <dq>‘Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as <dn>he</dn> inflicts a blemish upon <dn>him</dn>, so it is done to <dn>him</dn>.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And <dn>he</dn> who strikes a beast repays it, and <dn>he</dn> who strikes a man to death is put to death.</dq> [22] <dq>‘You are to have one right-ruling, for the stranger and for the native, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [23] And Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ěl, and they brought the one who cursed outside the camp, and stoned him with stones. And the children of Yisra’ěl did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh.

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Sabbatical Year
readings.subtitle: A Sabbath of Rest for the Land
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh on Mount Sinai, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, then the land shall observe a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six years you sow your field, and six years you prune your vineyard, and gather in its fruit,</dq> [4] <dq>but in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Do not sow your field and do not prune your vineyard.</dq> [5] <dq>‘Do not reap what grows of its own of your harvest, and do not gather the grapes of your unpruned vine, for it is a year of rest for the land.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the Sabbath of the land shall be to you for food, for you and your servant, and for your female servant and your hired servant, and for the stranger who sojourns with you,</dq> [7] <dq>and for your livestock and the beasts that are in your land. All its crops are for food.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Appointed Times and Sabbatical Laws
readings.title: The Year of Jubilee
readings.subtitle: Proclaiming Release Throughout the Land
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:8] <dq>‘And you shall count seven Sabbaths of years for yourself, seven times seven years. And the time of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.</dq> [9] <dq>‘You shall then sound a shophar-sound on the tenth day of the seventh new moon, on Yom haKippurim cause a shophar to sound through all your land.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall set <dn>את</dn> the fiftieth year apart, and proclaim release throughout all the land to all its inhabitants, it is a Yoḇel for you. And each of you shall return to <dn>his</dn> possession, and each of you return to <dn>his</dn> clan.</dq> [11] <dq>‘The fiftieth year is a Yoḇel to you. Do not sow, nor reap what grows of its own, nor gather from its unpruned vine.</dq> [12] <dq>‘It is a Yoḇel, it is set-apart to you. Eat from the field its crops.</dq> [13] <dq>‘In the Year of this Yoḇel let each one of you return to <dn>his</dn> possession.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when you sell whatever to your neighbour or buy from the hand of your neighbour, do not exploit one another.</dq> [15] <dq>‘According to the number of years after the Yoḇel you buy from your neighbour, and according to the number of years of crops <dn>he</dn> sells to you.</dq> [16] <dq>‘According to the greater number of years you increase its price, and according to the fewer number of years you diminish its price, because <dn>he</dn> sells to you according to the number of the years of the crops.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And do not oppress one another, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And you shall do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and shall do them. And you shall dwell in the land in safety,</dq> [19] <dq>‘and the land shall yield its fruit, and you shall eat to satisfaction, and shall dwell there in safety.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And since you might say, “What do we eat in the seventh year, since we do not sow nor gather in our crops?”</dq> [21] <dq>‘Therefore <dn>I</dn> have commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth the crop for three years.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall sow in the eighth year, and eat of the old crop until the ninth year. Eat of the old until its crop comes in.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And the land is not to be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is <dn>Mine</dn>, for you are sojourners and settlers with <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
